question_html: From which Latin words is the word 'company' derived, and what was its original literal reference?

options.A: 'Com' meaning with or together, and 'panis' meaning bread, originally referring to persons taking food together[cite: 26].
options.B: 'Com' meaning commerce, and 'panis' meaning money, originally referring to trade partners.
options.C: 'Compus' meaning corporate, and 'ny' meaning law, referring to legal entities.
options.D: 'Com' meaning group, and 'pany' meaning shares, referring to shareholders.

answer_html: Answer: (A) The word company is derived from 'com' (with or together) and 'panis' (bread), originally referring to an association of persons taking food together[cite: 26].

question_html: According to Justice Marshal, how is a corporation defined?

options.A: An association of merchants trading abroad with unlimited liability.
options.B: An artificial being, invisible, intangible and existing only in the contemplation of law[cite: 26].
options.C: A business organization created by the executive branch of government.
options.D: A voluntary partnership with perpetual succession.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Justice Marshal defined a corporation as an artificial being, invisible, intangible and existing only in the contemplation of law[cite: 26].

question_html: Which of the following is NOT a salient feature of a company?

options.A: Incorporated Association[cite: 26]
options.B: Status of a natural citizen[cite: 26]
options.C: Perpetual Existence[cite: 26]
options.D: Separate Legal Entity[cite: 26]

answer_html: Answer: (B) A company is not a citizen in the same sense as a natural person is, though it is created by the process of law[cite: 26].

question_html: Under the Companies Act, 2013, what is the current legal status regarding the use of a 'Common Seal' by a company?

options.A: It is compulsory for all companies to affix a common seal on all contracts.
options.B: The use of common seal has been made optional[cite: 26].
options.C: It has been completely abolished and declared illegal.
options.D: It is mandatory only for foreign companies operating in India.

answer_html: Answer: (B) The use of common seal has been made optional under the Companies Act, 2013; documents requiring it may instead be signed by two directors or one director and a company secretary[cite: 26].
topic_text: Common Seal and Corporate Identification Number

question_html: What is the unique identification number assigned to every company registered in India by the Registrar of Companies?

options.A: Permanent Account Number (PAN)
options.B: Corporate Identification Number (CIN)[cite: 26]
options.C: Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number (TAN)
options.D: Global Entity Identification Number (GEIN)

answer_html: Answer: (B) Every company registered in India is required to obtain a unique Corporate Identification Number (CIN) assigned by the Registrar of Companies[cite: 26].

question_html: According to Section 2(45) of the Companies Act, 2013, what is the minimum percentage of paid-up share capital that must be held by the Central Government and/or State Government(s) for a company to be classified as a Government Company?

options.A: Not less than 50%
options.B: Not less than 51%[cite: 26]
options.C: More than 50%
options.D: At least 75%

answer_html: Answer: (B) A Government company means any company in which not less than 51 per cent of the paid-up share capital is held by the Central Government, State Government(s), or partly by both[cite: 26].

question_html: How does Section 2(42) define a 'Foreign Company' under the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: Any company incorporated outside India that has a place of business in India (physically or through electronic mode) and conducts business activity[cite: 26].
options.B: Any company having more than 50% foreign shareholders regardless of its place of incorporation.
options.C: Any corporation registered abroad that holds investments in Indian subsidiaries.
options.D: Any company whose registered office is outside Asia.

answer_html: Answer: (A) A foreign company is any company or body corporate incorporated outside India which has a place of business in India (physically or electronically) and conducts business activity[cite: 26].

question_html: What is the maximum limit on the number of members for a private company under Section 2(68), excluding current and former employees who are/were members?

options.A: 50 members
options.B: 100 members
options.C: 200 members[cite: 26]
options.D: No limit

answer_html: Answer: (C) Except in case of One Person Company, a private company limits the number of its members to two hundred[cite: 26].

question_html: When two or more persons hold one or more shares in a private company jointly, how are they treated for the purpose of counting the maximum member limit of 200?

options.A: They are counted individually as separate members.
options.B: They are treated as a single member[cite: 26].
options.C: They are excluded entirely from the member count.
options.D: They are counted as half a member each.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Where two or more persons hold one or more shares jointly, they shall be treated as a single member for the purpose of the member limit[cite: 26].

question_html: What are the statutory financial thresholds to qualify as a 'Small Company' under Section 2(85) of the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: Paid-up capital not exceeding ₹4 crores and turnover not exceeding ₹40 crores[cite: 26].
options.B: Paid-up capital not exceeding ₹10 crores and turnover not exceeding ₹100 crores.
options.C: Paid-up capital not exceeding ₹2 crores and turnover not exceeding ₹20 crores.
options.D: Paid-up capital not exceeding ₹5 crores and turnover not exceeding ₹50 crores.

answer_html: Answer: (A) A small company has paid-up share capital not exceeding ₹4 crores (or higher up to ₹10 crores) and turnover not exceeding ₹40 crores (or higher up to ₹100 crores)[cite: 26].

question_html: Which of the following entities is explicitly EXCLUDED from qualifying as a 'Small Company' under Section 2(85), regardless of capital and turnover?

options.A: A holding company or a subsidiary company[cite: 26]
options.B: A private company with 50 members
options.C: A company limited by shares
options.D: An unlisted public company

answer_html: Answer: (A) Nothing in the small company clause shall apply to a holding company, a subsidiary company, a company registered under section 8, or a company governed by any special Act[cite: 26].

question_html: What is a 'Listed Company' as per Section 2(52) of the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: A company that has any of its securities listed on any recognised stock exchange[cite: 26].
options.B: A company whose shares are traded exclusively among promoters.
options.C: A public company with a paid-up capital of over ₹10 crores.
options.D: Any company registered with the SEBI database.

answer_html: Answer: (A) A listed company means a company which has any of its securities listed on any recognised stock exchange[cite: 26].

question_html: How is a 'Company limited by guarantee' defined under Section 2(21) of the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: A company having the liability of its members limited by the memorandum to such amount as the members respectively undertake to contribute to the assets of the company in the event of its being wound up[cite: 26].
options.B: A company where bank guarantees cover all short-term borrowings.
options.C: A company where directors guarantee the repayment of public deposits.
options.D: A company whose debentures are guaranteed by the Central Government.

answer_html: Answer: (A) A company limited by guarantee has the liability of its members limited by the memorandum to the amount undertaken to contribute upon winding up[cite: 26].

question_html: Under Section 2(87), when is a company deemed a 'subsidiary company' in relation to another holding company?

options.A: When the holding company controls the composition of its Board of Directors or exercises/controls more than one-half of the total share capital[cite: 26].
options.B: When the holding company owns at least 25% of its equity shares.
options.C: When the holding company guarantees its bank loans exceeding ₹1 crore.
options.D: When the companies share common directors.

answer_html: Answer: (A) A subsidiary company is one in which the holding company controls the composition of the Board of Directors or exercises/controls more than one-half of the total share capital[cite: 26].

question_html: According to Section 128 of the Companies Act, 2013, books of account must be kept on what basis and according to which system of accounting?

options.A: Cash basis and single entry system
options.B: Accrual basis and double entry system of accounting[cite: 26]
options.C: Hybrid basis and single entry system
options.D: Accrual basis and statement of affairs system

answer_html: Answer: (B) Every company shall keep books of account on accrual basis and according to the double entry system of accounting[cite: 26].

question_html: As per Section 2(40) of the Companies Act, 2013, financial statements of a company include which of the following?

options.A: Balance sheet, Profit and Loss account (or Income & Expenditure account), Statement of changes in equity, Cash flow statement, and Explanatory notes[cite: 26].
options.B: Balance sheet, Directors' report, and Auditors' report only.
options.C: Trial balance, Cash flow statement, and Fund flow statement.
options.D: Profit and loss account and Directors' responsibility statement only.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Financial statements include a balance sheet, profit and loss account/income & expenditure account, cash flow statement, statement of changes in equity, and explanatory notes[cite: 26].

question_html: Which types of companies are exempted from including a Cash Flow Statement in their financial statements under Section 2(40)?

options.A: Banking and Insurance companies
options.B: One Person Company, small company, and dormant company[cite: 26]
options.C: Private companies with less than 20 members
options.D: Section 8 charitable companies only

answer_html: Answer: (B) The financial statement with respect to One Person Company, small company, and dormant company may not include the cash flow statement[cite: 26].

question_html: According to the applicability of Divisions under Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013, which division applies to companies required to apply Accounting Standards notified under the Companies Act, 2013 (relevant for CA Foundation level)?

options.A: Division I[cite: 26]
options.B: Division II[cite: 26]
options.C: Division III[cite: 26]
options.D: Division IV

answer_html: Answer: (A) Division I applies to companies required to apply Accounting Standards notified under the Companies Act, 2013[cite: 26].

question_html: Under Schedule III Division II of the Companies Act, 2013, which entities are required to apply Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)?

options.A: Non-Banking Finance Companies (NBFCs)[cite: 26]
options.B: Companies required to apply Ind AS (other than NBFCs)[cite: 26]
options.C: Cooperative societies registered under state acts
options.D: Foreign companies having branches in India

answer_html: Answer: (B) Division II applies to companies that are required to apply Indian Accounting Standards notified under the Companies Act, 2013[cite: 26].

question_html: Which Division of Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013 prescribes the format for Non-Banking Finance Companies (NBFCs) required to apply Ind AS?

options.A: Division I
options.B: Division II
options.C: Division III[cite: 26]
options.D: Division IV

answer_html: Answer: (C) Division III applies to Non-Banking Finance Companies (NBFCs) that are required to apply Indian Accounting Standards[cite: 26].

question_html: In the Balance Sheet of a company prepared as per Schedule III Part I, under which major head and sub-head is 'Securities Premium' disclosed?

options.A: Shareholders' Funds under Reserves and Surplus[cite: 26]
options.B: Non-Current Liabilities under Other Long-Term Liabilities
options.C: Current Liabilities under Short-Term Provisions
options.D: Shareholders' Funds under Share Capital

answer_html: Answer: (A) Securities Premium is included under Reserves and Surplus within Shareholders' Funds[cite: 26].

question_html: Where are 'Bonds or Debentures' with a maturity period exceeding 12 months from the reporting date classified in a company's Balance Sheet?

options.A: Current Liabilities under Short-Term Borrowings
options.B: Non-Current Liabilities under Long-Term Borrowings[cite: 26]
options.C: Shareholders' Funds under Money received against share warrants
options.D: Current Liabilities under Other Current Liabilities

answer_html: Answer: (B) Bonds and debentures are classified under Long-Term Borrowings within Non-Current Liabilities[cite: 26].

question_html: Under which head in Schedule III Part I Balance Sheet are 'Provision for employee benefits like gratuity and provident fund' (payable after 12 months) categorized?

options.A: Long-term provisions under Non-current liabilities[cite: 26]
options.B: Short-term provisions under Current liabilities
options.C: Other current liabilities
options.D: Reserves and Surplus

answer_html: Answer: (A) Employee benefits provision like gratuity and provident fund are classified as Long-term provisions under Non-current liabilities[cite: 26].

question_html: Where must 'Current maturities of long-term borrowings' be disclosed in a company's Balance Sheet?

options.A: Under Long-Term Borrowings
options.B: Under Short-Term Borrowings[cite: 26]
options.C: Under Long-Term Provisions
options.D: Under Contingent Liabilities

answer_html: Answer: (B) Current maturities of long-term borrowings shall be disclosed separately under Short-Term Borrowings[cite: 26].

question_html: Unpaid dividends declared by a company are required to be classified under which head in the Balance Sheet?

options.A: Reserves and Surplus
options.B: Other Current Liabilities[cite: 26]
options.C: Short-Term Provisions
options.D: Short-Term Borrowings

answer_html: Answer: (B) Unpaid dividends are grouped under Other Current Liabilities[cite: 26].

question_html: Under Schedule III Part I, how are tangible assets officially designated on the asset side?

options.A: Fixed Assets
options.B: Property, Plant and Equipment[cite: 26]
options.C: Tangible Operating Assets
options.D: Physical Capital Assets

answer_html: Answer: (B) Tangible assets are designated as Property, Plant and Equipment under Non-current assets[cite: 26].

question_html: Which of the following items is classified as an 'Intangible Asset' under Schedule III?

options.A: Loose tools
options.B: Computer software[cite: 26]
options.C: Capital work-in-progress
options.D: Stores and spares

answer_html: Answer: (B) Computer software is classified as an Intangible asset[cite: 26].

question_html: Where should 'Investments in partnership firms' be disclosed if held as long-term investments?

options.A: Current Investments under Current Assets
options.B: Non-Current Investments under Non-Current Assets[cite: 26]
options.C: Long-Term Loans and Advances
options.D: Other Non-Current Assets

answer_html: Answer: (B) Investments in partnership firms are classified under Non-Current Investments[cite: 26].

question_html: Under which head are 'Loose tools' and 'Stores and spares' reported within Inventories?

options.A: Current Assets under Inventories[cite: 26]
options.B: Property, Plant and Equipment
options.C: Other Current Assets
options.D: Non-Current Investments

answer_html: Answer: (A) Loose tools and stores and spares form part of Inventories under Current Assets[cite: 26].

question_html: Where are 'Cheques, drafts in hand' and 'Cash in hand' presented in a company's Balance Sheet?

options.A: Other Current Assets
options.B: Cash and Cash Equivalents under Current Assets[cite: 26]
options.C: Short-Term Loans and Advances
options.D: Trade Receivables

answer_html: Answer: (B) Cheques, drafts in hand, and cash in hand are classified under Cash and Cash Equivalents[cite: 26].

question_html: In the Statement of Profit and Loss (Schedule III Part II), where must 'Earnings per equity share' (Basic and Diluted) be disclosed?

options.A: In the Notes to Accounts only
options.B: At the bottom of the Statement of Profit and Loss[cite: 26]
options.C: In the Directors' Report
options.D: In the Balance Sheet under Shareholders' Funds

answer_html: Answer: (B) Earnings per equity share (Basic and Diluted) is disclosed as item XVI in the Statement of Profit and Loss[cite: 26].

question_html: Is every public company necessarily a listed company?

options.A: Yes, all public companies must have their shares listed on a stock exchange.
options.B: No, every listed company is a public company, but every public company is not a listed company[cite: 26].
options.C: Only if its paid-up capital exceeds ₹50 crores.
options.D: Yes, unless exempted by the Central Government.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Every listed company is a public company, but every public company is not a listed company[cite: 26].

question_html: Under the Companies Act, 2013, what is the minimum paid-up share capital requirement for incorporating a private company or a public company?

options.A: ₹1,00,000 for private and ₹5,00,000 for public
options.B: No minimum paid-up capital requirement[cite: 26]
options.C: ₹10,000 for private and ₹1,00,000 for public
options.D: ₹50,000 for both private and public

answer_html: Answer: (B) The minimum paid-up share capital requirements of INR 1,00,000 and INR 5,00,000 have been done away with under the Companies Act, 2013[cite: 26].

question_html: What is a 'One Person Company' (OPC) defined as under Section 2(62) of the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: A company which has only one person as a member[cite: 26].
options.B: A company managed by a single sole proprietor without incorporation.
options.C: A company where all shares are owned by the Central Government.
options.D: A partnership firm converted into a corporate entity.

answer_html: Answer: (A) One Person Company means a company which has only one person as a member[cite: 26].

question_html: Does the death, insolvency, or change of members affect the legal existence and continuity of a company?

options.A: Yes, the company must be dissolved and re-registered.
options.B: No, because the company has perpetual existence independent of its members[cite: 26].
options.C: Yes, unless approved by the Registrar of Companies.
options.D: Only if all shareholders become insolvent simultaneously.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Since a company has existence independent of its members, it continues to be in existence despite the death, insolvency, or change of members (perpetual existence)[cite: 26].

question_html: What is the extent of liability of a shareholder holding fully paid-up shares in a company limited by shares?

options.A: Unlimited liability for all debts of the firm
options.B: Subject to no further liability[cite: 26]
options.C: Liability limited to the market value of shares on stock exchange
options.D: Joint and several liability with directors

answer_html: Answer: (B) If such shares are fully paid-up, the shareholder is subject to no further liability[cite: 26].

question_html: How are the rights of shareholders to inspect a company's books of account governed?

options.A: Solely by the provisions of the Indian Partnership Act
options.B: By the Articles of Association, with the exception of books open for inspection under the Statute[cite: 26]
options.C: At the discretion of the chief executive officer without restrictions
options.D: Shareholders have no statutory or internal right to inspect books

answer_html: Answer: (B) The right of shareholders to inspect books of account, except those open under statute, is governed by the Articles of Association[cite: 26].

question_html: According to Section 129 of the Companies Act, 2013, by whom must the financial statements be laid at every annual general meeting?

options.A: The Board of Directors of the company[cite: 26]
options.B: The statutory auditors
options.C: The Registrar of Companies
options.D: The managing director individually

answer_html: Answer: (A) The Board of Directors of the company shall lay financial statements at every annual general meeting of a company[cite: 26].
topic_text: Laying of Financial Statements at AGM

question_html: What is an 'Unlimited Company' as defined under Section 2(92) of the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: A company not having any limit on the liability of its members[cite: 26].
options.B: A company with unlimited authorized share capital.
options.C: A company allowed to operate without registration.
options.D: A company that can raise infinite public deposits.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Unlimited company means a company not having any limit on the liability of its members[cite: 26].

question_html: Can a private company that is a subsidiary of a public company be deemed a public company under the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: No, its private status in articles overrides everything.
options.B: Yes, a company which is a subsidiary of a company not being a private company shall be deemed to be a public company[cite: 26].
options.C: Only if approved by a special resolution of shareholders.
options.D: Only if its turnover exceeds ₹100 crores.

answer_html: Answer: (B) A company which is a subsidiary of a company, not being a private company, shall be deemed to be public company for the purposes of this Act even where such subsidiary company continues to be a private company in its articles[cite: 26].

question_html: In the presentation of Share Capital under Schedule III Part I, which of the following is NOT a required reconciliation disclosure for each class of share capital?

options.A: Number and amount of shares authorized[cite: 26]
options.B: Shares outstanding at beginning and end reconciled[cite: 26]
options.C: Personal income tax details of major shareholders
options.D: Calls unpaid and forfeited shares[cite: 26]

answer_html: Answer: (C) Personal income tax details of shareholders are never part of share capital disclosures under Schedule III[cite: 26].

question_html: Where are 'Capital redemption reserve' and 'Debenture redemption reserve' disclosed in the Balance Sheet?

options.A: Under Reserves and Surplus[cite: 26]
options.B: Under Long-Term Provisions
options.C: Under Non-Current Liabilities
options.D: Under Other Current Liabilities

answer_html: Answer: (A) Capital redemption reserve and debenture redemption reserve are sub-heads under Reserves and Surplus[cite: 26].

question_html: How must 'Long-term loans and advances' be sub-classified in terms of credit quality under Schedule III?

options.A: Secured considered good; Unsecured considered good; Doubtful[cite: 26]
options.B: Prime, Sub-prime, and Non-performing
options.C: Short-term, Medium-term, and Long-term
options.D: Domestic and International

answer_html: Answer: (A) Long-term loans and advances are sub-classified as secured considered good, unsecured considered good, and doubtful[cite: 26].

question_html: What is required regarding the periodic audit of a company's accounts?

options.A: Accounts must be periodically audited by chartered accountants appointed by shareholders on board recommendation[cite: 26].
options.B: Audit is optional if turnover is below ₹10 crores.
options.C: Internal employees can perform the statutory audit.
options.D: Audit reports are submitted directly to the stock exchange without shareholder involvement.

answer_html: Answer: (A) A company has to get its accounts periodically audited through chartered accountants appointed by shareholders on board recommendation[cite: 26].

question_html: Under Section 128, where can a company keep its books of account and financial statements?

options.A: At its registered office[cite: 26]
options.B: At the personal residence of the Managing Director[cite: 26]
options.C: At any branch office abroad without electronic linkage
options.D: At the office of the statutory auditor

answer_html: Answer: (A) Every company shall prepare and keep at its registered office books of account and other relevant books and papers[cite: 26].
topic_text: Place of Keeping Books of Account

question_html: What does 'Control over the composition of a subsidiary company's Board of Directors' mean under Section 2(87)?

options.A: Exercise of some power to appoint or remove all or a majority of the directors[cite: 26].
options.B: Power to audit executive compensation.
options.C: Right to veto dividend declarations.
options.D: Ownership of 25% voting rights.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Control over the composition of a subsidiary company's Board of Directors means exercise of some power to appoint or remove all or a majority of the directors[cite: 26].

question_html: Which of the following is a characteristic feature regarding the transferability of shares in a company?

options.A: Shares are freely transferable except in a private limited company which may have restrictions[cite: 26].
options.B: Shares can never be transferred under any circumstances.
options.C: Shares can only be transferred with court permission.
options.D: Shares of public companies are non-transferable.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Shares are transferable by its members except in case of a private limited company, which may have certain restrictions[cite: 26].

question_html: In the context of Schedule III Part II Statement of Profit and Loss, how are expenses categorized? Provide examples of major expense headings.

options.A: Cost of materials consumed, Purchases of Stock-in-Trade, Changes in inventories, Employee benefits expense, Finance costs, Depreciation and amortization expense, and Other expenses[cite: 26].
options.B: Operating and non-operating expenses only.
options.C: Fixed and variable manufacturing costs.
options.D: Direct material, direct labor, and factory overhead.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Schedule III Part II expenses include cost of materials consumed, purchases, changes in inventories, employee benefits, finance costs, depreciation, and other expenses[cite: 26].
topic_text: Statement of Profit and Loss Expenses Headings

question_html: What is the status of an unlisted public company if its shares are later unlisted or if it was never listed?

options.A: It converts automatically into a private company.
options.B: It continues to be a public company[cite: 26].
options.C: It becomes a dormant company under Section 455.
options.D: It dissolves unless registered as an OPC.

answer_html: Answer: (B) A company which is a listed public company if it gets unlisted continues to be a public company[cite: 26].

question_html: Which of the following describes the separation of ownership and management in a company?

options.A: Shareholders elect a board of directors to carry out operational management through it[cite: 26].
options.B: Shareholders manage day-to-day operations directly at registered offices.
options.C: Directors own all the shares of the company by law.
options.D: Management is handled exclusively by debenture trustees.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Shareholders are authorized by law to elect a board of directors and, through it, to act as a separate legal entity, separating ownership from day-to-day management[cite: 26].
